# util-nd - n-d iteration and copy machinery

Paths are relative to `jix/src/` unless prefixed. Release builds have overflow checks OFF (unchecked
`*`/`+` wrap silently); CI tests only x86_64, while i686 and armv7 wheels ship untested (see util-memory.md).

## Purpose

The engine every read path bottoms out in. `NdCopier` (util/nd_copy.rs) moves a rectangular n-d region
between two byte buffers with independent non-negative byte strides, specialized by `(itemsize, alignment)`.
`NdIterUnordered<I, N>` / `NdIterUnorderedDyn<I>` drop unit dims, sort dims by stride, coalesce contiguous
runs and drive a 1-d inner loop with one offset per operand (consumers: NdCopier, the elementwise pipeline,
select, reductions). `NdIter` (util/iter/nd.rs) is the ordered C-order walker over `[begin, end)` with
pluggable extensions (stride offsets, logical global index, block border offset/size). `arr_ext.rs` builds
and maps fixed arrays inline with drop guards; `arr_sequence.rs` adapts `[Array;N]`, `&[Array;N]`,
`Vec<Array>`, `&[Array]` and 1-10 tuples to stack / concatenate / map_multiple. All strides are unsigned
(bytes, or elements for `(1,1)` layouts); negative strides never reach this code.

## Contracts

### NdCopier (util/nd_copy.rs:14-438)
- `new(dtype)` (29-39) picks by `(itemsize, alignment)`: (1,1) u8, (2,2) u16, (4,4) u32, (8,4) [u32;2],
  (8,8) u64, (16,8) [u64;2]; anything else (itemsize 3, 12, 24, 0, align 16, (4,2)) -> `copy_untyped`
  (byte-wise). Struct dtypes have no padding since #88, so typed copies of structs read no uninit bytes (K3).
- `unsafe copy(src, dst, shape, src_strides, dst_strides, dtype)` (57-105), Safety doc 46-55: (1) each
  wrapped slice covers `sum (shape[d]-1)*stride[d] + itemsize` bytes from its start; (2) src and dst regions
  do not overlap; (3) `dtype` has the (itemsize, alignment) given to `new` - only debug_asserted
  (116-117); `copy_untyped` sizes elements from copy's `dtype` (387) (K54, documented in #90).
- Pre-pass (66-92, NEW in c28c62a #103): any len 0 -> return before any pointer math; count dims with
  len > 1. 0 long dims (incl. 0-d `[]`, any shape length) -> shape `[1]`, strides `[0]` (one element);
  1 long dim d -> re-slice shape and both stride slices to `[d..d+1]` (bounds-checked: panics if a stride
  slice is shorter than d+1); >= 2 -> original slices go to the iterator path.
- Implicit: `src_strides.len() == dst_strides.len() == shape.len()` is asserted only on the iterator path
  (nd_iter_unordered.rs:70-72). With <= 1 long dim, longer stride slices are accepted silently.
- dst may contain 0-stride (repeated) positions: last-writer-wins, sequential writes, not UB.
- Alignment is never trusted from the dtype: ALIGNED kernels only when both base pointers (119) and the
  strides actually used (1-d: 135-137; n-d: every post-coalesce stride, 157-158) are multiples of
  `align_of::<T>()`. NdCopier does not consult `REQUIRE_ALIGNED`; unaligned kernels are always valid.
- Scalar routes: `pick_inner_loop` (182-236) gets flags computed from the same strides the kernel then
  receives (1-d 139-146; n-d 157-178, where `foreach_inner_1d` passes `iter.inner_strides()`).
- Span responsibility is the caller's: storage/compact.rs:419-517, storage/buf.rs:268-287
  (`StridedBuf::copy_from`), array/compact.rs:212 and 315-324, ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:515-588
  (Staging), ops/shape_ops/tile.rs:157-292, flip.rs:146-165, repeat.rs:142-203, ops/sub_dtype.rs:103-120,
  util/bench_util.rs:20.

### fill_contiguous (nd_copy.rs:440-470)
- `pub(crate) unsafe fn` with NO Safety doc. Real contract: `src` valid for `itemsize` reads, `dst` non-null
  and valid for `n*itemsize` writes, no overlap (built via `PtrNoalias::new` / `PtrMutNoalias::new`, i.e.
  `from_raw_parts`). Typed arms read `*src` even when n == 0 (312); the untyped arm returns at n == 0 (361).
  Only caller: `Staging::fill_from` (ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:528-545), where n = chunk_len >= 1.

### NdIterUnordered<I, N> / NdIterUnorderedDyn<I> (nd_iter_unordered.rs:34-331, _dyn.rs:16-246)
- `I` is usize or u64 (u64 in the reduction). Input: `shape: &[I]`, per-operand strides (each asserted to
  have `shape.len()`, 70-72 / _dyn 32-35), per-operand `(size, alignment)` in that operand's stride unit.
  At most NDIM_MAX dims of len > 1 (DimArray push panics otherwise).
- Provides: every element visited exactly once with all operands' offsets paired for the same logical
  element (multiset equality with a C-order walk: `assert_visits` 446-463, props 687-733).
- Order: len-1 dims dropped (78-85); dims sorted by stride descending, operand 0 most significant; a 0
  stride abstains (113-115); a pair no operand can compare returns `None`, which `dims_sort_by` (312-331,
  arm 322) treats as transparent. `new_with` (64-172) excludes operands from the sort, but they still
  constrain coalescing. Nesting order is UNSPECIFIED; along any single input dim the index increases.
- Coalescing (131-152; _dyn 94-116): consecutive sorted dims merge iff for EVERY operand
  `s[group_inner] == s[d] * shape[d]` (unchecked mul); group stride = innermost member's, len = product.
- Flags (155-164): `is_strides_aligned[i]` = every post-coalesce stride % alignment == 0; it says nothing
  about the base pointer (callers check it: nd_copy.rs:119, ops/elementwise/select.rs:159-164,
  ops/reduction/common.rs:697-699). `is_contiguous[i]` = inner stride == size.
- Sentinels: all-len-1 or 0-d -> shape [1], strides FAKED to `size`, flags true (86-96); empty -> shape
  [0], strides `size`, flags true (174-188); a single long dim keeps its real stride, no sort (98-103).
- `foreach_inner_1d(f)` (213-218): `f(offsets, inner_len, inner_strides)`, inner_len and inner_strides
  constant per iterator. ndim 1 -> exactly one call with zero offsets, INCLUDING the empty sentinel (len 0)
  (228-231). 2-d uses a manual loop (276-290), >= 3-d an `NdIter` over the outer dims (291-304), with the
  closure dyn-dispatched unless `foreach_inner_1d_impl::<true>` (pub(super); NdCopier 168, 425).
- Dyn variant: same algorithm, Vec tables, slices lent, no `new_with`; 0 operands -> everything coalesces.
- Consumers: nd_copy.rs:152, 417; ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:220 (<= 16 operands incl. output), 347
  (dyn, above 16); select.rs:149; reduction/common.rs:674 (`new_with`, u64, 3rd operand = logical reduced
  index, excluded from the order), 1158 (finalize; out and state buffers may alias), 1177 (empty reduction).

### NdIter and extensions (iter/nd.rs:13-519, iter/strides.rs:9-172)
- C-order walk over `[begin, end)` per dim, u64 coordinates; asserts lengths, `begin <= end` and
  `check_ndim` (49-57). 0-d yields exactly one item; any empty dim yields none (`nitems`, 59 and 66).
- Notification protocol (193-200): a step's changes arrive right-to-left (wrapped dims as `on_decrease`
  back to begin, then the incremented dim); the last step also reports the run-off-the-end wrap.
  reduction/common.rs:525-546 relies on row-major tile order ("folded front-to-back").
- Stride offset exts (strides.rs:9-157): `offset += S::from_u64(diff) * stride[dim]`; `from_u64` is a
  truncating `as` (util/mod.rs:87-89); offsets are relative to the walk start and never underflow (a
  decrease returns a dim to its begin). `nd_iter_ext_logical_global_index` (160-172): C-order linear index
  over `shape`, initial offset from `begin`.
- Extension list capped at 3: merging a 4th resolves to `()` and hits `unimplemented!` (nd.rs:370-379;
  documented 212-213, 396). Real usage is at most 2.

### NdIterExtBlockOffsetSize (iter/block.rs:22-141)
- Requires NdIter bounds `[begin/b, calc_block_end(begin, end, b))` per dim (doc 9-16; calc_block_end is
  util/mod.rs:620-629) and every `b >= 1` (div by zero at 59-65).
- Per dim: low border `(begin%b, min(b - begin%b, end - begin))`; high border index `end/b` with offset 0
  (or `begin%b` when it is the low block) and size `end%b - offset`; interior `(0, b)`. If `end % b == 0`
  the high index equals block_end and is never visited.
- Callers: storage/compact.rs:466-481, array/read.rs:525-537, array/compact.rs:247-253 and 278-286
  (`builder(grid)` with begin 0 - equivalent), reduction/common.rs:443-453 and 531-546.

### arr_ext.rs
- `array_try_from_fn_inline` (12-58): on Err/panic drops exactly the initialized prefix (InitGuard 27-55)
  when `T: Drop`. `array_try_map_inline` (61-98) / `array2_try_map_inline` (115-164): each source item is
  moved out at most once; `next` is advanced before `f` runs, so a panicking `f` owns its item; the
  unconsumed tail is dropped by DropGuard.

### arr_sequence.rs
- `ArraySequenceImpl` (60-74): `arr < narrays()` else panic (index; tuples via
  `out_of_bounds_array_index`, 723-727). `narrays() == 0` is representable for Vec, slices, `[_; 0]`;
  map.rs:237, stack.rs:66, concatenate.rs:73 reject it (K87 fixed).
- `read_data` (CHANGED in c28c62a #103 / 7ebac4c #104): forwards `&Index` and `OutBuf<'_, 'a>` unchanged to
  `self[arr].storage.read_data` and returns `Result<()>`; the push/pull contract is the inner storage's.
- `ElementwisePipelineTuple::N_OPERANDS` (124) must EXACTLY equal what `operands()` yields:
  ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:136-140 fills `[&Operand; N]` with `unwrap()` (too few -> panic) and only
  debug_asserts leftovers (too many -> the extra operands never get a cursor in release). Formulas: 219 and
  316 (`count * N`), 420 and 542 (None), 678 (sum).
- `read_bulk_as_iter` (140-150) Safety: that of `ElementwisePipelineImpl::read_bulk` (pipeline.rs:51-56, fn at 56)
  plus: drop the returned iterator and its items before the next call (Vec/slice reuse an `UnsafeCell`
  scratch). Only caller: ops/elementwise/map.rs:349-366 (consumed in place; `F` is higher-ranked over the
  item lifetime, so items cannot escape).

## Unsafe inventory

- nd_copy.rs:104 fn-pointer dispatch - relies on copy()'s contract (caller; non-local).
- nd_copy.rs:126-129 single-element read/write_unaligned; 404 untyped single element - span >= itemsize.
- nd_copy.rs:146, 168-178, 411, 425-436 inner-loop calls through `bytes_offset` (util/mod.rs:710, 764:
  `get_unchecked(offset..)`, needs offset <= slice len). Local part: every yielded offset <= span -
  itemsize; caller part: the span (non-local).
- nd_copy.rs:250-251, 308 `assert_unchecked(CONTIG == (stride == size_of::<T>()))` - local: established by
  pick_inner_loop receiving the same flags/strides (see Contracts). A mismatch is release UB.
- nd_copy.rs:257, 259-263 contiguous `copy_nonoverlapping` (needs non-overlap: caller); 266-279 strided
  loops; 296-297 `[T; LEN]` move needs len == LEN (debug_assert 291; const arms are picked from that len).
- nd_copy.rs:312-320 broadcast reads src once even for len 0; 340, 345, 369-375 untyped copies; the
  doubling fill copies dst -> dst with `n <= filled` (disjoint halves; local).
- nd_copy.rs:441-469 `fill_contiguous` - whole contract on the caller, undocumented.
- util/mod.rs:686-691, 734-739 `Ptr*Noalias::new` (caller) - shared with util-memory.md.
- nd_iter_unordered*.rs, iter/*: no unsafe, but every consumer's pointer math trusts their offsets.
- arr_ext.rs:24, 52, 57 (write / assume_init), 34-39 (drop prefix), 70, 93, 128-130, 158-159 (`ptr::read`),
  83, 145-146 (drop tail) - local, guarded.
- arr_sequence.rs:239-241, 336-338, 449-450, 571-572, 690 `read_bulk` - caller (map.rs) establishes.
- arr_sequence.rs:444, 566 `&mut *UnsafeCell::get()` - relies on the "drop before next call" rule (non-local,
  map.rs:349-366). 447/452/456 and 569/574/578: `spare_capacity_mut` + `MaybeUninit::write` +
  `set_len(narrays * M)` - sound since #93 (K124) because each `read_bulk` returns `[T; M]`.

## Edge-case surface

- Empty: NdCopier returns at 70; NdIterUnordered calls the closure once with len 0; NdIter yields nothing.
  Storage impls only debug_assert non-empty (pipeline.rs:211, 335; shape ops); empties are filtered at
  array/read.rs:207, 296, 366, 433.
- 0-d / all-unit: NdCopier pre-pass copies one element; NdIterUnordered gives one run of len 1 with faked
  strides; NdIter yields one empty index.
- Length-1 dims are dropped whatever their stride (0, huge, unaligned) by both the pre-pass and the iterator.
- 0 strides: src broadcast kernels (300-322, 351-376); dst 0-stride repeated writes; 0-stride dims abstain
  from the sort; 0/0 pairs coalesce. The pipeline turns dims where every operand has stride 0 into len 1
  before building the iterator (pipeline.rs:201-209).
- Permuted layouts: NdCopier's own tests never use permuted/F-order strides or a 0-stride dst (fuzz at
  703-741 is C-order with gaps); NdIterUnordered props do cover permutations (706).
- NDIM_MAX=8: carry ladder 7..0 (nd.rs:84); `dim_arr` asserts ndim <= 8 (dimension.rs:494). Tile/Repeat add
  a synthetic dim and require ndim < NDIM_MAX (tile.rs:59, repeat.rs:43).
- itemsize: typed 1/2/4/8/16; 3, 12, 24, 0 untyped. `Itemsize` is u16 (dtype.rs:124); `Alignment` is a
  power of two below 2^16 (dtype.rs:42-96).
- 32-bit: on i686 `align_of::<u64>() == 4` while scalar dtypes declare 8 (dtype.rs:950-968), so the
  debug_assert at nd_copy.rs:117 panics in debug builds for (8,8)/(16,8) copies (K8, open); release picks
  kernels from `align_of::<T>()` and is correct. `Idx::from_u64` truncates; regions are bounded by
  `check_region_size` on 32-bit (settled in batch5).
- Overflow (release wraps): coalescing `s[d] * shape[d]` (139; _dyn 102), `group_len *=` (142), NdIter
  `nitems` (59) and `remaining()` (145-146). Settled for current callers: every walk is a sub-region of a
  shape that passed `check_shape_overflow` (error.rs:192; zeros counted as 1 in `try_shape_product`).
- Block iteration: partial low/high edge blocks, single-block ranges, begin == end (aligned or not),
  end % b == 0.
- Aliasing: NdCopier forbids src/dst overlap (no caller was found to violate it); reduction finalize
  (reduction/common.rs:1157-1172) walks out and state that may alias at the same offsets.

## Intentional behaviors

- NdIterUnordered visit order is unspecified; tests compare as a multiset (doc 8-31; assert_visits 446-463).
- An empty region still calls the inner loop once with len 0 (228-231; test comment 588-591). The doc
  "visits nothing" (47-49) means no element; the harness comment at 404 ("inner_calls == 0") is inexact.
- A zero stride abstains from the order (test 840); an excluded operand still constrains coalescing
  (test 868); an ambiguous comparison is transparent (test 884).
- Unit dims never block coalescing, whatever stride they carry (nd_copy.rs tests 766-788).
- NdCopier chooses aligned kernels at runtime and tests misaligned bases (551-647); broadcast src along any
  axis (842-875); `fill_contiguous` for itemsizes 1..24 incl. odd (877-893); zero extent is a no-op (690, 895).
- The struct field-by-field copier was removed in 763a701 (#72). The type doc is current (nd_copy.rs:6-13,
  fixed in #105); test comments still name `copy_1d` / "struct-field pointer" (670, 688-689) - stale names.
- NdIter 0-d yields one empty index (iter/nd.rs test 582); notification order is tested (820-890).
- Out-of-range `arr` on a tuple sequence panics (arr_sequence.rs:723-727).
- `REQUIRE_ALIGNED` is false on x86/x86_64/aarch64 (util/mod.rs:653-657): unaligned typed access is allowed
  there by design.
- [CONFIRMED in batch7-3 as K164 (fixed-size arrays abort a 2 MiB stack from N ~ 490-1300); tuples not yet checked] `MAX_ITEMSIZE` of `[Array<S>; N]` / tuple sequences ignores N (219-220, 679): judged unrealistic in batch5.
- Pipeline `N_OPERANDS` dispatch: up to 16 operands (incl. output) are const-generic, above that
  `NdIterUnorderedDyn` (pipeline.rs:88-111; _dyn test 423).

Older, still worth a look:

  dims merge when the bijection fails for some operand? A 60k-case randomized check passed in batch5.
- Sentinel consumers: does every `foreach_inner_1d` consumer tolerate the len-0 call and the FAKED strides

- Callers' spans: for every NdCopier call site, is the slice at least `strided_span_bytes(shape, strides,
